newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds quiet, just slightly tighter.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds quiet, just slightly tighter.

text.p: With no clear signs of direction, U.S. mortgage-backed securities largely treaded water on Monday, traders said.
Spreads over Treasuries were mostly steady to a hair's breadth wider.
"We lost a little ground on Friday, so we're probably going to get a little of that back today," one trader said. "It's
Demand for pass-throughs remained strong, with at least one dealer seen collecting them for collateralized mortgage obligation (CMO) production.
Late on Monday, mortgage were unchanged to off 3/32.

Specifically, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5-percent paper was off 1/32 at 100-21/32 bid, yielding 103 basis points over 10-year Treasuries. Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac issues also were off 1/32, at 100-16/32 and 100-21/32, respectively.
The 10-year note was off 2/32 to yield 6.41 percent.
Mortgages appeared to be awaiting a cue from Treasuries, which were on hold pending economic data and the Treasury's quarterly refunding effort, traders said.
"We're not going to get much direction this week, except maybe downward," one trader said.
